svg.title: How an Arabian Sea marine heatwave can fuel extreme monsoon rain
svg.desc: Three map panels of the Arabian Sea, India and Pakistan. Panel 1: during a dry, clear spell of the summer monsoon, extra sunshine and slack winds warm two hotspot regions, the eastern and northern Arabian Sea, into a marine heatwave. Panel 2: the warm water heats and moistens the air above it and a counter-clockwise low-level cyclone forms over each warm patch, with clouds and rain over the sea that then cool the water. Panel 3: the cyclone pushes moist ocean air onshore, onto southwest India near Kerala for eastern heatwaves and onto Pakistan and northwest India for northern ones, where extreme rain becomes two to three times as likely; offshore winds leave the coast farther north drier. A bar beneath reads: the atmosphere drives the ocean, then the ocean drives the atmosphere.
